key_insight: ScienceBuddy turns everyday researcher interactions into a built-in learning loop, so scientific AI agents can keep improving while being used. Its core idea is "recursive-in-recursive self-improvement": the system improves both the agent's behavior and the environment/rubrics used to train it.
problem_solved: Scientific AI assistants often fail to improve from real research workflows because user requests, feedback, and execution traces are not systematically converted into learning signals. This paper addresses the gap between interactive use and continual model improvement in scientific tasks.
method: Builds ScienceBuddy, an interactive research workspace where scientists can delegate tasks and receive agent assistance in their normal workflow.
Converts user requests, feedback, and execution evidence into structured tasks and evaluation rubrics for continual learning.
Uses recursive-in-recursive self-improvement by combining harness evolution with model reinforcement learning to improve both the training setup and the agent itself.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to deploy agents that get better from real-world scientific use instead of static benchmarks alone. It could make research assistants more reliable, adaptive, and aligned with actual researcher needs.

paper_title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
